primary.title: Commentarii de Bello Gallico
primary.author: Julius Caesar
primary.rationale: Caesar's own account of his campaigns in Gaul, a foundational text for understanding his military career and political ambitions.

primary.title: Commentarii de Bello Civili

primary.title: The Gallic Wars
primary.author: Julius Caesar

secondary.title: Caesar: A Life

secondary.title: The Roman Revolution
secondary.author: Ronald Syme
secondary.rationale: While older, Syme's work is a seminal study of the transition from Republic to Empire, with significant analysis of Caesar's role. Its influence warrants its inclusion, though it predates the 1976 cutoff.

secondary.title: Julius Caesar: The Lost Hero
secondary.author: Barry Strauss
secondary.rationale: A recent scholarly biography that offers a fresh perspective on Caesar's life and legacy.

suggestions.notes: While Caesar's speeches are known through the writings of others (e.g., Cicero), direct primary source texts authored by him are primarily his commentaries on his military campaigns. Ronald Syme's 'The Roman Revolution' is included despite its age due to its foundational status in understanding the period, though newer scholarship is also provided.
